answer: Under Section 34 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, nothing is considered an offence if it is done in the exercise of the right of private defence. This right applies to both the defence of one's body and property. The right of private defence commences when there is a reasonable apprehension of danger and continues as long as that apprehension exists. Additionally, the right extends to situations where the defender may risk harm to an innocent person while exercising this right (Section 44). Furthermore, the right of private defence of property can include the voluntary causing of death or harm to a wrong-doer under certain conditions (Section 41).
summary_answer: The right of private defence under Section 34 allows individuals to act in self-defense without it being considered an offence, specifically for the protection of body and property.
